## Shared scenes

> The Ashdown children sit in the old [Methodist](../codex/factions.md#methodist) cemetery talking about gravestones, ghosts, and the [Carrow](../character/carrow.md) family. Drawn by the smell of cooked trout, they run down to [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow) and join the [Carrow](../character/carrow.md) children for supper, quickly becoming fast friends.
>

> Led by the smell of cooked trout, Tobias, [Grace](../character/grace.md), [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md), and [Rupert](../character/rupert.md) join the [Carrow](../character/carrow.md) children in [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow) for a meal. They share stories of their lives and neighbors, quickly becoming fast friends before returning to their respective homes.
>

> The Ashdown children find a runaway girl named [Mary Stubbs](../character/mary-stubbs.md) hiding in an old barn near their home. They feed her and listen as she shares her tragic past, her escape from her abusive guardian, and her unique perspectives on life and religion.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS P4](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0004), [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS P14](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0014), [v5 CHAPTER V. > [Mary Stubbs](../character/mary-stubbs.md) attends church with the manse children using borrowed clothes, making a scene by sticking her tongue out at a parishioner. Refusing to attend school, she cleans the manse, spars with [Aunt Martha](../character/aunt-martha.md) over food, and spends time with the local children at [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow). Despite occasional arguments, Mary captivates the children with her stories, ghost tales, and unique tricks.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE P8](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0008), [v5 CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE P9](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0009), [v5 CHAPTER VI. > Miss Winifred interrogates Mary at the manse and later updates [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) and [Tabitha](../character/tabitha.md) after learning that Mrs. [Grimble](../character/grimble.md) has died. Meanwhile, the children gather at [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow), where Edmund reads myths and imagines the Pied Piper leading them away. [Bess](../character/bess-carrow.md) arrives with news of Mrs. Grimble's death, startling Mary, but [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) reassures her and promises to pray that Mary can remain in [Seven Gulls](../codex/places.md#seven-gulls).
>

> Miss Winifred urges Mr. Ashdown to address Mary's upbringing, leading Mr. Ashdown to speak warmly with the girl. Driven by Mary's impending return to the asylum, [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) visits Miss Winifred to ask if she will take Mary in. After consulting her husband [Ambrose](../character/ambrose.md), Miss Winifred agrees to adopt Mary, and the children give Mary farewell gifts.
>

> Mary and [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) converse about faith and the possibility of Mr. Ashdown remarrying, which leaves [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) frightened and tearful. Meanwhile, [John Ashdown](../character/john-ashdown.md) reads through the night and contemplates his late wife, oblivious to Ida's distress.
>

> [John Ashdown](../character/john-ashdown.md) becomes engrossed in [German](../codex/factions.md#german) theology, neglecting his duties and family. Mrs. Hector Twiss visits the manse and proposes adopting [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md), but Ashdown firmly rejects her offer. Outraged, Mrs. [Twiss](../character/twiss.md) criticizes his parenting before departing, leaving Ashdown deeply shaken and introspective.
>

> Mrs. [Twiss](../character/twiss.md) leaves the manse after scolding the children and Mr. Ashdown. Disturbed by her accusations about his parenting, Mr. Ashdown reflects on his children's needs and decides to seek company and comfort by visiting [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) and [Harriet Ainslie](../character/harriet-ainslie.md).
>

> [Mary Stubbs](../character/mary-stubbs.md) joins [Grace](../character/grace.md), [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md), [Bess](../character/bess-carrow.md), and [Izzy](../character/izzy.md) in [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow) to chew spruce gum. [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) feels envious of Mary's fine new clothes and muff, while Mary brings news of local gossip and mentions that [Aunt Martha](../character/aunt-martha.md) killed a rooster for dinner. Horrified that their pet rooster [Adam](../character/adam.md) has been killed, [Grace](../character/grace.md) rushes home, prompting [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) to repentantly give Mary her gum and compliment her muff.
>

MARY BRINGS EVIL TIDINGS P32](../source/v05-c18.md#nw-v05-c18-p0032)_

> [Grace](../character/grace.md) is furious and heartbroken after [Aunt Martha](../character/aunt-martha.md) slaughters her pet rooster, [Adam](../character/adam.md), to serve to the visiting minister, Mr. Perry. During dinner, [Grace](../character/grace.md) openly dislikes Mr. Perry, who eats [Adam](../character/adam.md) and preaches at her. Later in the study, [Grace](../character/grace.md) secretly watches Mr. Perry's coat-tails catch fire from the hearth, getting revenge on him when he scorches his new coat.
>

> [Mary Stubbs](../character/mary-stubbs.md) scolds the manse children in the graveyard for their misbehavior and the gossip it causes, revealing rumors that their father might marry [Clementine Ainslie](../character/clementine-ainslie.md). After Mary leaves, [Kit Carrow](../character/kit-carrow.md) arrives and suggests they start a [Good-Conduct Club](../codex/factions.md#good-conduct-club) to manage their behavior and avoid bringing shame on their father.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XXIII. THE GOOD-CONDUCT CLUB

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER XXIII. THE GOOD-CONDUCT CLUB P3](../source/v05-c23.md#nw-v05-c23-p0003), [v5 CHAPTER XXIII. THE GOOD-CONDUCT CLUB P33](../source/v05-c23.md#nw-v05-c23-p0033), [v5 CHAPTER XXIII. > At Kit's suggestion, [Grace](../character/grace.md) and her siblings decide to form the [Good-Conduct Club](../codex/factions.md#good-conduct-club) to self-regulate their behavior and avoid bringing shame on their father. After writing up their agreement and signing it in the cemetery by lantern light, [Grace](../character/grace.md) and [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) go to bed and discuss Mary Stubbs's warnings about stepmothers and the rumor about Miss Ainslie.
>

> In an impulse of charity, [Grace](../character/grace.md) gives her only good shoes and stockings to barefoot [Zilla Marsh](../character/zilla-marsh.md), who quickly leaves to preserve her new possessions. Realizing she will now have to wear her hated striped stockings to church, [Grace](../character/grace.md) stands barefoot in a snowbank to catch a cold so she can legitimately stay home. [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) and Tobias pull [Grace](../character/grace.md) off the ice after a loud struggle that onlookers misinterpret as a fight, though [Grace](../character/grace.md) wakes up healthy the next morning still determined not to wear the stockings.
>

> [Grace](../character/grace.md) scandalizes the congregation by wearing boots without stockings to church, drawing sharp criticism from local gossips while [Tabitha](../character/tabitha.md) and the Carrow girls rush to her defense. To protect her father's reputation and fulfill a punishment imposed by Tobias, [Grace](../character/grace.md) publishes an explanatory letter in the local newspaper detailing why she gave away her last good stockings.
>

> [Winifred](../character/winifred-tolley.md), [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md), [Tabitha](../character/tabitha.md), and Hugh discuss the manse children's disruptive graveyard concert during the [Methodist](../codex/factions.md#methodist) prayer meeting and Winifred's conversation with their father. Afterwards, Mr. Ashdown summons his children to his study to confront them about the incident. Remorseful, the children promise to punish themselves through their club, while Mr. Ashdown laments his perceived failings as a father.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XXVII. A SACRED CONCERT

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER XXVII. A SACRED CONCERT P1](../source/v05-c27.md#nw-v05-c27-p0001), [v5 CHAPTER XXVII. A SACRED CONCERT P10](../source/v05-c27.md#nw-v05-c27-p0010), [v5 CHAPTER XXVII. > The [Good-Conduct Club](../codex/factions.md#good-conduct-club) decides to fast on Sunday as punishment for their graveyard song, which causes [Ida Ashdown](../character/ida-ashdown.md) to faint during the church service. Doctor [Hugh Carrow](../character/hugh-carrow.md) and Mrs. Elder Clow help revive her, leading [Grace](../character/grace.md) to explain their self-punishment rule to their distraught father. Realizing how neglected his children are, [John Ashdown](../character/john-ashdown.md) reflects mournfully on his duties as a father and his unresolved love for [Clementine Ainslie](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) before returning to his theological studies.
>

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY P0](../source/v05-c28.md#nw-v05-c28-p0000), [v5 CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY P11](../source/v05-c28.md#nw-v05-c28-p0011), [v5 CHAPTER XXVIII. > While spending a pleasant spring evening at [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow), the children share their dreams for the future until [Mary Stubbs](../character/mary-stubbs.md) arrives and startles them with a ghost story about [Henry Warren](../character/henry-warren.md) and the nearby ruined [Bailey](../codex/places.md#bailey) property. After Mary cooks trout for the group, darkness falls and the lingering terror forces [Grace](../character/grace.md), [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md), and [Rupert](../character/rupert.md) to head home together, carefully avoiding the old garden.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XXIX. A WEIRD TALE

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER XXIX. A WEIRD TALE P0](../source/v05-c29.md#nw-v05-c29-p0000), [v5 CHAPTER XXIX. A WEIRD TALE P1](../source/v05-c29.md#nw-v05-c29-p0001), [v5 CHAPTER XXIX. A WEIRD TALE P9](../source/v05-c29.md#nw-v05-c29-p0009), [v5 CHAPTER XXIX. A WEIRD TALE P14](../source/v05-c29.md#nw-v05-c29-p0014)_

> Terrified by a white figure crawling in the [Bailey](../codex/places.md#bailey) garden that they mistake for Henry Warren's ghost, [Grace](../character/grace.md), [Rupert](../character/rupert.md), and [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) flee from [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow) to [Hollowmere](../codex/places.md#hollowmere). [Clementine Ainslie](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) calms the children while [Tabitha](../character/tabitha.md) goes to investigate with a pitchfork. [Tabitha](../character/tabitha.md) returns with the news that the 'ghost' was merely old Mrs. [Stimson](../character/stimson.md) crawling around in white sheets searching for a lost knitting needle.
>

> Tobias punishes [Rupert](../character/rupert.md) for running away from a ghost by forcing him to sit on a graveyard tombstone until midnight. [Rupert](../character/rupert.md) endures the chilly rain during his midnight vigil and subsequently falls gravely ill with double pneumonia. After a tense battle for his life, [Rupert](../character/rupert.md) recovers with the support of the community and returns to [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow).
>

> [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) and Miss Winifred discuss the upcoming marriages of [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) Ashdown and [Harriet Ainslie](../character/harriet-ainslie.md), as well as plans for the minister's children while he is away. Meanwhile, the local children gather outdoors on Kit's final night before leaving for Regent's [Academy](../codex/places.md#regent-s-academy), where Edmund imagines the Pied Piper calling the boys away to follow him.
